_comment: ConEd SC1 residential rates. Edit + redeploy to update the tool with no code change. app.js fetches this and overrides the defaults baked into calc.js. Cents are expressed as $/kWh; demand rates are $/kW. Each plan also carries display metadata (name, basis, eligibility, ratesAsOf, source) and its published eligibility/lock-in rules (requires, lockIn, solar, smartChargeConflict) that the eligibility engine and plan-by-plan comparison surface.

meta.asOf: Standard/TOU: 2025 published SC1 NYC averages. TOU & demand rates: current as of 2026-07.
meta.switchTiming: A rate switch takes effect with a future meter read — typically your next bill or the one after (1–2 billing cycles).

standard.name: Standard Residential
standard.eligibility: every SC1 residential customer (the default rate)
standard.ratesAsOf: 2025 published SC1 NYC averages (2026 usage priced at 2025 rates); PDF verified 2026-07

tou.name: Time-of-Use
tou.eligibility: SC1 residential customers who opt in
tou.ratesAsOf: residential TOU supply rates current as of 2026-07

lockIn.note: one-year minimum on TOU (ESCO-supplied homes exempt); leave and you can't rejoin TOU for 18 months

smartChargeNY.name: SmartCharge NY
smartChargeNY.eligibility: what-if only — Con Edison currently says Residential Time-of-Use customers are not eligible

steadyUse.name: Steady Use Rate

lockIn.note: cancel anytime without penalty, but you can't re-enroll for 18 months after opting out

steadyUse.solar: ConEd says solar / net-metering homes are likely not a good fit for the Steady Use Rate — Standard or Time-of-Use may suit you better.
steadyUse.smartChargeConflict: Enrolling in Steady Use automatically unenrolls you from SmartCharge NY.

smartEnergy.name: Smart Energy Plan

lockIn.note: cancel anytime without penalty, but you can't re-enroll for 18 months after opting out

smartEnergy.solar: ConEd does not recommend the Smart Energy Plan for solar customers (its billing structure works against net metering) and suggests the Net Metering Plan instead.

bill.basis: ConEd 3-Year Historical Average Full Service Electric Rates — NYC Residential SC 1, grossed up for GRT + sales tax, excluding customer charge & BPP

accuracy.basis: docs/product-strategy.md 'Accuracy gate': charge only when ≥95% of complete, supported billing periods reconcile within passPct of the actual bill

pricing.basis: docs/product-strategy.md 'Pricing' + 'Accuracy gate': $29 report only when projected first-year savings exceed $150 (measured at the low end of the range); never charged until the 20-account backtest certifies the model and a payment provider is wired
